newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota stadium bill seen in two to three weeks.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota stadium bill seen in two to three weeks.

text.p: A bill for a new Minnesota Twins baseball stadium is expected to be drafted in two to three weeks, a Minneapolis-St. Paul official said Friday.

Bill Lester, executive director of the Metropolitan Sports Facilities Commission, which is heading negotiations on the stadium, said that attorneys for the commission were working with legislative staff to draft a bill.

He said there would be some state funding for the approximately $300 million ballpark that could be accomplished in part through bond issuance. However, he said that property, sales and income taxes were not being considered for the project. Instead, hotel, cigarette or car rental taxes may be examined, he added.

On Wednesday, the Pohlad family, which owns the Twins, proposed giving Minnesota a 49 percent stake in the baseball team in return for the state's assistance in financing the stadium. The team, meanwhile, would contribute more than $157.5 million in construction and operating costs.
Lester said more detail was needed on what he termed was an "unprecidented" offer by the Twins owners.
A report in the Star Tribune quoted Gov. Arne Carlson as saying it "sounds like a very reasonable offer."
Meanwhile, a bill sponsored by U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moyhihan, D-New York, that would bar the use of tax-exempt bonds for professional sports stadiums is still lurking in the future.
Last week, an aide to the senator said a bill would be reintroduced on Jan. 21 with an effective date of when the Senate Finance Committee votes on the measure.
Lester said he was aware of the bill and that taxable bonds could be considered for the Twins ballpark.
